path.name: Software Systems with AI Agents
path.description: A live program where builders use Claude Code, Codex, and other AI agents to design real software systems, then prove the work by shipping a real system for a real organization, sourced from an actual RFP.
path.targetAudience: CS students, coding bootcamp participants, self-taught builders, and career switchers who want to become software system architects. No formal enrollment required, just comfort writing and reading code.

programs.name: How to Create Software Systems with AI Agents
programs.description: A two-week live cohort, Monday through Thursday, where builders use Claude Code, Codex, and other AI agents to design real software systems: databases, APIs, and architecture, then ship a system built live for a real organization, sourced from an actual RFP.
programs.learningOutcomes: Set up and direct AI coding agents responsibly, engineer prompts and context for real projects, design relational and graph data models, build and query APIs, document architecture with Mermaid diagrams, review and debug AI-generated code, read and respond to a real RFP, and ship a working system for a real organization.
programs.projectSummary: A real software system you design and ship in response to an actual RFP or civic problem: a working data model, API, and application, built with AI agents and documented like production work.
programs.portfolioArtifact: Your Git repository with the shipped system, commits, architecture notes and Mermaid diagrams, the RFP research and outreach draft, and a final reflection on what the agents got right, what they got wrong, and what you fixed.
programs.cohortNote: New cohorts run every so often. The next cohort opens Monday, August 17, 2026 and runs two weeks, Monday through Thursday, 6:00 PM-7:30 PM CST. The same build-session rhythm keeps running afterward in the AutoNateAI Discord as Live Builds, every Saturday, 10:00 AM-12:00 PM CST, open to the whole community.

sessions.name: Session 1: Meet Your AI Agents
sessions.objectives: Set up Claude Code and Codex as real collaborators and learn to point an agent at an unfamiliar codebase before asking it to change anything.
sessions.liveActivity: Install and configure Claude Code and Codex, walk through a real repository together, and have an agent explain its architecture, entry points, and data flow back to you.
sessions.homework: Use an agent to map a small existing codebase and write a short architecture note describing its components and how they connect.

sessions.name: Session 2: Prompt and Context Engineering in Practice
sessions.objectives: Apply prompt and context engineering to a real multi-file project: structure the ask, and give the agent only the context it actually needs.
sessions.liveActivity: Take a real feature request, structure a prompt with role, task, and constraints, hand the agent the relevant files, and review the diff line by line.
sessions.homework: Use an agent to implement one small feature in an existing project and document what context you gave it, what you accepted, and what you rejected.

sessions.name: Session 3: Databases and APIs
sessions.objectives: Design a relational schema for a real problem, wire up a simple API, and use an agent to scaffold both responsibly.
sessions.liveActivity: Design tables, keys, and relationships for a sample system, build API endpoints against them, and query the data live.
sessions.homework: Add one table and one API endpoint to a project, and write the query that answers a real question about the data.

sessions.name: Session 4: System Architecture and Mermaid Diagrams
sessions.objectives: Turn a working system into a diagram: use Mermaid to communicate architecture and organize services and components.
sessions.liveActivity: Pick a real system, diagram it in Mermaid, identify its weak points, and talk through tradeoffs with an agent.
sessions.homework: Produce a Mermaid architecture diagram for your own project and one paragraph explaining a tradeoff you made.

sessions.name: Session 5: Debugging and Reviewing AI-Generated Code
sessions.objectives: Build the habit of reviewing agent output like a senior engineer: reading diffs, running tests, and catching hallucinated logic.
sessions.liveActivity: Review a batch of AI-generated changes live, find at least one real bug or hallucination, fix it, and commit the working version.
sessions.homework: Review and correct one AI-generated change in your own project, documenting what was wrong and why.

sessions.name: Session 6: Reading a Real RFP With AI
sessions.objectives: Find and read an actual government or foundation RFP, and use an agent to extract requirements, stakeholders, and constraints.
sessions.liveActivity: Pull a live RFP, have an agent summarize it, and identify who issued it and what problem it's really asking to solve.
sessions.homework: Find one real RFP or civic problem and write an agent-assisted summary of what it's asking for and who it would help.

sessions.name: Session 7: Build Week Part 1 - Design and Start the Real System
sessions.objectives: Turn the researched RFP into an actual system design and start building it live.
sessions.liveActivity: Design the architecture for the chosen system, scaffold the repository, and implement the first real feature with agent support.
sessions.homework: Keep building: commit progress and update the architecture notes as the design changes.

sessions.name: Session 8: Build Week Part 2 - Ship It
sessions.objectives: Finish a working version of the system, write it up, and identify who to contact about it.
sessions.liveActivity: Finish the build, demo it live, and draft outreach identifying the people or organization who should see it.
sessions.homework: Submit final repo link, architecture notes, a short system writeup, and the outreach draft.
